question: Spot the correct spelling of an REE-bearing metamorphic texture term.
solution:
The correct answer is** option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Correct term:** *Porphyroblastic* — adjective describing a metamorphic texture in which relatively large crystals (porphyroblasts) are set in a finer-grained matrix.
 
• **Meaning:** A *porphyroblast* is a conspicuously larger mineral grain that grew during metamorphism; porphyroblastic rocks show these large crystals surrounded by a finer groundmass.
 
• **Context (REE-bearing):** Some porphyroblasts (e.g., garnet, monazite) can concentrate rare earth elements (REEs) and are therefore important in petrogenetic and geochemical studies.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• *Prophyroblastic* — incorrect spelling (extra initial "o").
 
• *Porfyroblastic* — incorrect (missing "h").
 
• *Porphyroblastik* — incorrect ending ("-ik" is nonstandard).
